speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I see you're an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To begin narrowing down the cause, have you noticed any specific patterns in your fractures, such as them occurring from minor trauma or falling from standing height?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency (a form of Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia).

The combination of virilizing features (clitoromegaly, acne, maternal hirsutism), sexual infantilism (delayed menarche, partial fusion), and bone fragility is classic for this condition. I recommend ordering a 17-hydroxyprogesterone and aldosterone/renin activity panel to confirm.
